summary:
The Florida Freeze Disaster Assistance Act of 2026 makes a supplemental appropriation to the Department of Agriculture to fund State-administered disaster assistance for specified agricultural losses attributable to freeze or cold weather conditions.

Section 1 provides the short title. Section 2 appropriates, out of amounts in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $3,500,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, as an additional amount for the “Office of the Secretary” of the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The appropriation is no-year funding, to remain available until expended. The funds are for the Secretary of Agriculture to provide assistance in the form of block grants to States for losses of revenue, quality, or production of crops, including crops prevented from planting, and of trees, bushes, and vines, when such losses are a consequence of a freeze or cold weather condition.

Section 2 imposes several conditions and limitations on the availability and use of the funds. The assistance must include compensation to producers for losses of multi-year crops. Funds are available exclusively for losses occurring in counties that received a disaster designation for freeze and related cold weather conditions issued by the Secretary on March 4, 2026. Funds are to be made available upon the request of a State department of agriculture or another appropriate State agency as determined by the Secretary.

Section 2 also establishes a reporting requirement: not later than 120 days after enactment, and for each fiscal quarter thereafter until the appropriated amounts are expended, the Secretary must submit a report to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations describing implementation of the assistance provided under the Act. The $3.5 billion appropriation is designated by Congress as an emergency requirement under section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985. The bill does not amend the United States Code or authorize future appropriations; it directly appropriates the specified amount.
